warnings.title: ESC mid-click re-selects: the drag-release click-select never checks press_swallowed
warnings.location: app/main.odin:332-337 (ESC latch) vs app/main.odin:488-494 (drag-release click-select) vs app/main.odin:524 (plain-release, gated)
warnings.evidence: app/main.odin:337: "app.press_swallowed = true // an in-flight click's release must not re-select after ESC"; app/main.odin:491-494: "moved := rl.Vector2Distance(mouse, app.press) > 6\nif !moved && !release_ui_hit(app, mouse) {\n    click_select(app, mouse)"; app/main.odin:524: "} else if rl.IsMouseButtonReleased(.LEFT) && !app.press_swallowed {"
warnings.detail: ESC deselect sets press_swallowed but leaves drag.active set; the drag-branch release click-selects without the latch, so press-on-node -> ESC -> release-without-move re-selects the node, contradicting the code's own comment and the PR interaction map.
warnings.recommended_fix: Gate the drag-branch click-select on !app.press_swallowed (match the plain-release branch), or clear app.drag.active in the non-placing ESC branch.

warnings.title: Placement commit lacks release_ui_hit: a 6px chip-boundary press+release places a router under the tray
warnings.detail: The click-select releases gate on release_ui_hit (the 6px-boundary gap) but the placement commit checks only press_swallowed: press 1-5px outside a chip edge, release onto the chip -> moved<=6 -> router placed on the map tile under the tray band, where the player aimed at the chip (cancel intent).
warnings.recommended_fix: Add a tray-chip hit check (release_ui_hit's chip loop) to the placement commit condition at app/main.odin:510, mirroring the click-select release gate.

warnings.title: App-layer input glue (click_select/popover_click/release_ui_hit/press_swallowed/dispatch/toasts) has zero automated coverage
warnings.evidence: harness/run.odin:13-14: "import pp \"../core\"\nimport rnd \"../app/render\""; grep for click_select/popover_click/release_ui_hit/press_swallowed across *_test.odin: zero references; demos demolish_bundle.dem:29 / demolish_node.dem:31 lower demolish intents straight into the action log (harness/demo.odin:458-460).
warnings.detail: No test drives the surface dispatch or its reject toasts; the demos pin the underlying command stream (same command kinds, validate->apply->log, replay byte-identity). Matches repo precedent: 3.2 r1 rated the dial/lane-keys/toast zero-coverage a warning and 3.5 r1 rated placement input paths a note - both READY TO MERGE.
warnings.recommended_fix: Add headless app-layer tests for selection priority, swallow latch, X/DEL dispatch and toasts when the input logic is extracted testable; the demos+replay already pin the command stream.
warnings.verification: confirmed (severity regraded from the lens's blocker per repo precedent 3.2/3.5)

notes.title: PR interaction map claims the right+left chord swallows its release; the code deliberately lets it click-select
notes.detail: The code re-anchors the chord press (press_swallowed=false) so its release DOES click-select — the PR body sentence is inaccurate for the chord. Docs-only; behavior is deliberate and sensible.
notes.recommended_fix: Correct the PR body sentence: ESC and the drag-interrupting right-click swallow their release; the chord re-anchors so its release click-selects from the chord position.

notes.title: Node-demolish reject toast has no render path (toast draws only inside the sel_pipe >= 0 block)
notes.evidence: app/main.odin:1022: "if app.sel_pipe >= 0 {"; app/main.odin:1062-1063: "if app.last_reject != .None && app.tick - app.reject_tick < 30 { // ~1.5s at 20Hz\ndraw_text(app, reject_label(app.last_reject), 12, 156, 16, rl.Color{200, 60, 60, 255})"
notes.detail: A .Missing_Node / .Terminal_Demolish rejection keeps sel_node >= 0 with sel_pipe == -1, so the belt-and-braces toast never renders. Unreachable through the UI today (only live junctions are selectable), but the spec's error-handling row has no visible surface.
notes.recommended_fix: Draw the reject toast outside the sel_pipe block (gated only on last_reject freshness) so node-demolish rejections also surface.

notes.title: popover_rect final min-clamps can push x/y negative on windows smaller than the panel, contradicting its comment
notes.detail: With win_w < POPOVER_W+16 (226px) or win_h < h+TRAY_CLEAR, the final min() yields negative x/y (e.g. h=92, win_h=120 -> y=-18), contradicting the adjacent 'never overflow a small window' comment.
notes.recommended_fix: Re-apply lower guards after the final mins: y = max(8, min(y, f32(v.win_h)-h-8)); x = max(8, min(x, f32(v.win_w)-POPOVER_W-8)).

notes.title: Pipe popover anchor midpoint is computed twice (app + render) against the file's single-source claim
notes.evidence: app/main.odin:671: "pipe_anchor :: proc(app: ^App, ps: u32) -> rl.Vector2 {"; app/main.odin:676: "return {(a.x + b.x) / 2, (a.y + b.y) / 2}"; app/render/popover.odin:91: "anchor := rl.Vector2{(a.x + b.x) / 2, (a.y + b.y) / 2}"; app/render/popover.odin:10-12: "// Layout is owned HERE ... the app hit-tests the SAME rects\n// this package draws"
notes.detail: The rect math (popover_rect/demolish_button_rect) is single-sourced, but the pipe anchor formula lives in both packages; an asymmetric edit would silently drift hit-test vs draw. The node anchor is single-sourced via node_screen.
notes.recommended_fix: Export the pipe anchor from render/popover.odin and call it from the app's hit-tests and draw, like node_screen.

notes.title: Popover draws before draw_hud and can clamp to y=8 under the top-left HUD block, hiding its button while hit-testable
notes.location: app/main.odin:215-219 (popover draw) + draw_hud top-left block (title 12,10 / instructions 12,36 / score 12,56 / legend 12,76 / QoS readout 12,96+); app/render/popover.odin:44-45 (y<8 -> y=8, x<8 -> x=8)
notes.detail: An entity near the screen top-left anchors the popover at (8,8); draw_hud paints after, covering the panel/button (pipe popover button at y 36..62 sits under the instructions/score text) while the button stays hit-testable — an invisible-but-clickable demolish.
notes.recommended_fix: Draw the popover after draw_hud, or clamp the popover below the top-left HUD band.
